title: The Quiz We Lost Beautifully
scene: At a neighborhood pub quiz, a confident team discovers the other players know much more. A wildly wrong guess and a last-place finish earn them a bowl of chips, which they accept as a perfectly edible prize.
sceneJa: 近所のパブのクイズ大会に、少し自信満々で参加した友人たち。周りは次々に正解するのに、自分たちはお菓子の数すら大外れ。最下位の景品はポテトチップス一皿だったが、案外悪くない夜になった。

chunks.en: We signed up for a pub quiz
chunks.ja: パブのクイズ大会に申し込んだ

chunks.en: thinking we knew a bit of everything,
chunks.ja: 自分たちは何でもそこそこ知っていると思って

chunks.en: which turned out to be optimistic.
chunks.ja: それはずいぶん楽観的な見込みだった
2ラウンド目になるころには

chunks.en: the other teams were answering in seconds,
chunks.ja: ほかのチームは数秒で答えていて

chunks.en: and we didn't stand a chance.
chunks.ja: 僕らに勝ち目はなかった

chunks.en: We guessed there were forty sweets
chunks.ja: お菓子は40個だと予想した

chunks.en: in the jar on the counter,
chunks.ja: カウンターの瓶の中に
でも見当違いもいいところだった

chunks.en: and I said, "In our defense, we brought pencils."
chunks.ja: 僕は「言い訳すると、鉛筆はちゃんと持ってきた」と言った

chunks.en: The host gave us a bowl of chips
chunks.ja: 司会者がポテトチップスを一皿くれた

chunks.en: and my friend said, "I'll take it."
chunks.ja: 友人は「それなら喜んでもらうよ」と言った
まあ、せめてもの話だけど

chunks.en: with a prize we could eat.
chunks.ja: 食べられる景品をもらえたチームは

questions.question: Which split keeps 'didn't stand a chance' together as one meaning chunk?
options: By the second round / the other teams were answering in seconds / and we didn't stand / a chance.
By the second round / the other teams were answering in seconds / and we didn't stand a chance.
By the second round / the other teams were answering / in seconds and we didn't / stand a chance.
questions.explanation: 'Didn't stand a chance' is one useful expression meaning there was no realistic possibility of winning. Do not split 'stand' from 'a chance'.

questions.question: What does 'we were way off' mean about the sweets guess?
options: Their estimate was nowhere near the correct number.
They had guessed the exact number.
They refused to make any guess.
questions.explanation: 'Way off' means far from correct. It describes a badly inaccurate guess, not a small error.

questions.question: Why does the friend say 'I'll take it' about the chips?
options: They want to return the prize immediately.
They think the chips prove they won the quiz.
They are happy to accept a small consolation prize despite losing.
questions.explanation: 'I'll take it' accepts what's offered. Here the friend treats an edible last-place prize as a funny little victory.

speak: Imagine: you enter a friendly quiz with friends and feel confident. Read: follow the mood from confidence to embarrassment to cheerful acceptance. Chunk: practise 'didn't stand a chance', 'way off', and 'I'll take it' as whole units. Understand: the first describes low odds, the second a very wrong guess, and the third acceptance of an offer. Check: answer all three questions. Speak (30 seconds): tell a story about a game or contest where you were confident, got something badly wrong, and still found a small upside. Reuse 'In our defense' to make a light excuse. Final Read: read all six sentences aloud, stress 'didn't stand a chance', pause before 'way off', and say 'I'll take it' with a relaxed, amused tone.
review: New: 'didn't stand a chance'（勝ち目がなかった）, 'we were way off'（予想が大きく外れた）, 'I'll take it'（それならありがたく受け取る）. Reuse 'In our defense' (Lesson 108) and 'For what it's worth' (Lesson 111) in a new setting of losing a trivia game and finding a small consolation. Reviewed Lessons 103–116: unlike mistaken cheering, film confusion, Halloween surprise, or birthday planning, this story uses self-deprecating acceptance after a friendly competition. Usage sources: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/stand-a-chance ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/off-base ; https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/take_1
